name: Historic City of Sucre
description: Sucre, Bolivia's constitutional capital, sits high in the south-central Andes at about 2,790 metres. Its centre of whitewashed colonial streets is among the best preserved in the Americas. Founded by the Spanish in the 1500s, it still has early churches and convents, such as San Francisco and Santo Domingo, where European styles mix with local building traditions. It is also home to the country's Supreme Court.
